summary.headline: Revenue of $77,678 beat the weekly target at 113.6% attainment, while orders slipped 1.5% week on week and the year stays behind target.

points.what: Weekly gross revenue was $77,678, up 4.0% on the prior week and up 92.4% year on year.
points.so_what: This sits above the 8-week average of $68,426 and outside the 8-week range, so it is a notably strong revenue week.

points.what: Orders came in at 980, down 1.5% from 995 last week but up 84.6% year on year.
points.so_what: Year-on-year growth of 84.6% is above the 75% growth the targets assume, so the small weekly dip leaves the annual pace intact.

points.what: Both weekly targets were beaten: orders at 106.9% of target and revenue at 113.6% of target.
points.so_what: The week added $9,300 of revenue above target, helping close the year-to-date shortfall.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is $1,527,483, or 96.3% of the target to date, a gap of $57,991.
points.so_what: Despite the strong week, the full-year target of $3,888,802 still requires catch-up over the remaining 28 weeks.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate of 9.4% refers to the mature week of 01 Jun 2026; the two most recent weeks are not yet mature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be judged yet, so this rate should be read as a two-week-old signal.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 1.7 pp to 14.5%, a move at or above the 1.0 pp notable threshold and rated good.
points.so_what: At $908 of revenue per percentage point of cancellations, this shift is worth watching for whether it holds.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $811,926, just 100.1% of target, with $72,160 still needed in the final week of the quarter.
points.so_what: With one week left, the quarter's outcome depends on a week close to the $73,167 revenue target.

points.what: Weekly orders of 980 were 63 above the target of 917 (106.9%), and revenue of $77,678 was $9,300 above its $68,378 target (113.6%).
points.so_what: The week was ahead on both measures, against next week's targets of 952 orders and $73,167 revenue.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 100.1% of target at $811,926, with $72,160 remaining against the full-quarter target of $884,086.
points.so_what: The quarter is only marginally ahead, so the final week decides whether 2026-Q2 lands on target.

points.what: Year-to-date attainment is 96.3% and the required weekly run-rate for the rest of the year is $84,333 versus a current 8-week run-rate of $70,390.
points.so_what: At the present pace the $3,888,802 full-year target is out of reach, as May and June are the only months ahead of target so far.

points.what: LATAM orders fell 18.0% to 137, a contribution of -30 orders and 200% of the total weekly change.
points.so_what: LATAM alone more than accounts for the 15-order decline, with other regions partly offsetting it.

points.what: Search orders dropped 6.1% to 683, contributing -44 orders, or 293.3% of the weekly change.
points.so_what: Search carries 69.7% of all orders, so its direction sets the overall order trend.

points.what: EMEA rose 16.4% to 192 orders (+27) and Organic rose 21.1% to 161 orders (+28).
points.so_what: These gains cushioned the declines, and all four regions remain up year on year.

points.what: Average order value reached $92.69, up 3.5% on the week and 4.0% year on year, outside its 8-week range.
points.so_what: Higher value per order explains how revenue rose 4.0% while orders fell 1.5%.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved to 14.5%, down 1.7 pp from 16.2% and 0.2 pp below last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $908 of revenue, so this improvement supports the week's revenue beat.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 01 Jun 2026 was 9.4%, up 0.1 pp on the prior week and 0.2 pp year on year.
points.so_what: Both movements are rated bad, though the changes are small and not marked as notable.

points.what: New customer signups were 241, down 0.4% on the week and down 11.4% year on year, while orders grew 84.6% year on year.
points.so_what: Order growth is not being matched by new customer growth, which is a point to monitor for future demand.

summary.headline: Revenue hit $77,678, up 4.0% and 13.6% ahead of the weekly target, while orders eased 1.5%; the year remains behind target at 96.3%.

points.what: Weekly gross revenue reached $77,678, up 4.0% week on week and outside its 8-week range, against an 8-week average of $68,426.
points.so_what: Revenue came in 113.6% of the weekly target, a $9,300 cushion against next week's $73,167 target.

points.what: Orders fell 1.5% to 980 from 995, but were 84.6% above the same week last year.
points.so_what: That growth is above the 75% the targets assume, and orders still landed 106.9% of the weekly target of 917.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $811,926, or 100.1% of the target to date, with one week left in 2026-Q2.
points.so_what: Reaching the full-quarter target of $884,086 requires $72,160 in the final week.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue of $1,527,483 is 96.3% of target, a shortfall of $57,991.
points.so_what: A strong week does not change the year position, which remains behind target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate of 9.4% refers to the mature week of 01 Jun 2026; the two most recent weeks are not yet mature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be judged yet, so read this rate as an earlier-week signal.

points.what: New customer signups were 241, down 11.4% against the same week last year and down 0.4% week on week.
points.so_what: Signups are shrinking year on year while orders grow 84.6%, so order growth is not coming from new account creation.

points.what: Quarter-to-date attainment is only 100.1%, leaving $72,160 to be earned in the last week of the quarter.
points.so_what: That required amount is close to this week's $77,678, so the quarter target is within reach but not secured.

points.what: Orders reached 106.9% of the weekly target (980 vs 917) and revenue 113.6% (%$77,678 vs $68,378), both ahead.
points.so_what: Next week's bar rises to 952 orders and $73,167 revenue.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $811,926 against a target to date of $810,919, ahead by $1,007.
points.so_what: With one week left, $72,160 more is needed to reach the full-quarter target of $884,086.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is behind at 96.3% of target, and the remaining $2,361,319 over 28 weeks needs $84,333 per week.
points.so_what: The recent 8-week run-rate of $70,390 is below that required pace, so the full-year target of $3,888,802 is at risk.

points.what: LATAM orders fell 18.0% to 137, a contribution of -30 orders and 200% of the total weekly change.
points.so_what: LATAM alone more than accounts for the 15-order decline, with other regions partly offsetting it.

points.what: Search orders dropped 6.1% to 683, contributing -44 orders, or 293.3% of the change, while Organic added 28 orders, up 21.1%.
points.so_what: Search remains 69.7% of all orders, so its direction sets the weekly total despite Organic's gain.

points.what: EMEA rose 16.4% to 192 orders (+27) and APAC edged up 0.7% to 455, while North America fell 7.1% to 196.
points.so_what: Every region is still above last year, with EMEA up 106.5% and North America up 48.5%.

points.what: Average order value rose 3.5% to $92.69, above its 8-week range and 4.0% higher than last year.
points.so_what: Higher value per order explains how revenue grew 4.0% in a week when orders fell 1.5%.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved 1.7 pp to 14.5%, down from 16.2% and below last year's 14.7%.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $908 of revenue, so this move supports the week's revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 01 Jun 2026 was 9.4%, up 0.1 pp on the prior week and 0.2 pp on last year.
points.so_what: Returns are edging up slightly, and they are not deducted from the reported gross revenue figure.

points.what: New customer signups were 241, down 0.4% week on week and down 11.4% year on year.
points.so_what: Customer acquisition is not keeping pace with the 84.6% year-on-year growth in orders.
